Getting started

  1. Add Frost.Byte to a server where you have Manage Server: invite the bot. Its slash commands appear on their own.
  2. Switch on the modules you want. Run /module list to see them all and /module enable <name> to turn one on, or flip its switch on the dashboard. A module's setup command works while the module is still off, so you can configure it first.
  3. Fine-tune on the web. Log in to the dashboard with Discord, pick the server, and set channels, roles, messages and limits for each module.
  4. Check what members see. /help lists only the commands that member can run and that are switched on.

Who can run what

Everyone
Any member, in a server where the command's module is on.
Moderators
Members with the moderator permissions the command asks for, or a moderator role set with /modconfig.
Admins
Members with Manage Server. Discord hides these commands from everyone else, and the bot checks again.

Moderation & Safety

Keep the server safe with moderation tools, automatic filters, audit logs and member verification.

MdModeration

Ban, kick, timeout and warn with case history and escalation.

On when the bot joins. Turn it off with /module disable moderation. Set it up with /modconfig.

Settings and their defaults
SettingDefaultWhat it does
DM members when punishedOnMembers get a direct message when they are warned, timed out, kicked or banned.
Command visibilityPublicWho sees the confirmation of a moderation command.
  • /banModerators

    Ban a user, optionally for a set time

  • /caseModerators

    View or edit a moderation case, or list or clear a member's infractions.

    • /case view View a case.
    • /case reason Change a case's reason.
    • /case proof Set a case's proof link.
    • /case history List a member's moderation cases
    • /case clear-history Pardon all of a member's active warnings
  • /kickModerators

    Kick a member from the server

  • /modconfigAdmins

    Moderator settings: escalation, immune and mod roles, mute role, case log, visibility.

    • /modconfig escalation add Add or update a tier: N warnings within a period, then an action.
    • /modconfig escalation remove Remove an escalation tier.
    • /modconfig escalation list List the escalation tiers.
    • /modconfig immune add Make a role immune.
    • /modconfig immune remove Remove a role from the immune list.
    • /modconfig immune list List the immune roles.
    • /modconfig modroles add Give a role moderator access.
    • /modconfig modroles remove Remove a moderator role.
    • /modconfig modroles list List the moderator roles.
    • /modconfig muterole Set, create or clear the mute role (used for mutes over 28 days).
    • /modconfig logchannel Set or clear the channel for moderation case logs.
    • /modconfig visibility Who sees moderation command replies
    • /modconfig dm Turn DMs to punished members on or off.
    • /modconfig show Show the current moderation settings.
  • /purgeModerators

    Bulk-delete recent messages in this channel

  • /slowmodeModerators

    Set or remove a channel's slowmode

  • /softbanModerators

    Ban and instantly unban a user to delete their recent messages.

  • /timeoutModerators

    Time out a member; over 28 days uses the mute role

  • /unbanModerators

    Lift a ban by user ID

  • /unmuteModerators

    Remove a member's timeout or mute role

  • /warnModerators

    Warn a member; warnings can trigger automatic actions

AmAuto-Moderation

Automatically removes or punishes bad words, spam, invites, links, caps, mass mentions and more.

Off until you run /module enable automod or flip its switch on the dashboard. Set it up with /automod.

Configured with its commands and the lists on the dashboard.

  • /automodAdmins

    Auto-moderation rules, actions and exemptions

    • /automod enable Turn automod on. Your rules and lists stay as they are.
    • /automod disable Turn automod off. Rules and lists are kept.
    • /automod status Show every rule with its action and scope, the lists and the exemptions.
    • /automod rule Set a rule's action, threshold and scope (Bad Words, Caps, Anti-Spam, …).
    • /automod words add Add words or phrases (comma-separated).
    • /automod words remove Remove a word or phrase.
    • /automod words list List the filtered words (only you can see the list).
    • /automod patterns add Add a case-insensitive regex pattern.
    • /automod patterns remove Remove a regex pattern.
    • /automod patterns list List the regex patterns (only you can see the list).
    • /automod domains add Add a domain to the blocked or allowed list.
    • /automod domains remove Remove a domain from the blocked and allowed lists.
    • /automod domains list Show the blocked and allowed domains.
    • /automod exempt add Add a role and/or channel to the exemptions or to a rule's list.
    • /automod exempt remove Remove a role and/or channel from the exemptions or a rule's list.
    • /automod honeypot add Make a channel a honeypot, or create one.
    • /automod honeypot remove Stop a channel being a honeypot (the channel is kept).

LgAudit Logs

Posts message, member, voice, channel, role and server events to your log channels.

Off until you run /module enable logging or flip its switch on the dashboard. Set it up with /logging.

Configured with its commands and the lists on the dashboard.

  • /loggingAdmins

    Audit logs: turn on/off, pick log channels, toggle events

    • /logging enable Turn audit logging on.
    • /logging disable Turn audit logging off (settings are kept).
    • /logging status Show log channels, disabled events and ignored channels.
    • /logging channel Set or clear the channel for a log type.
    • /logging event Turn one log event (or all) on or off.
    • /logging ignore add Stop logging message events in a channel or category.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 19 October 2026

This policy covers the Discord bot and its web dashboard. They are run by one person, the bot owner, not by a company. Questions or requests: .

What the bot stores

The bot keeps only what its features need, in a database on the bot owner's own server:

  • Server settings that server staff choose: which modules are on, channels, roles, messages, embeds, custom commands, automations, panels and similar.
  • Discord IDs of servers, channels, roles, messages and members, so the bot knows where and to whom a feature applies.
  • Feature data about members, only for features a server turns on:
    • levels and XP, message counts and voice minutes
    • economy balances, items and boosts
    • achievements
    • birthdays (day and month, and the year only if you give it)
    • your time zone, if you set one
    • poll votes and giveaway entries
    • who invited whom, and when members joined or left
    • ticket owners and the reason you give when opening a ticket
    • temporary voice channel owners
    • captcha checks (a hashed answer and attempt count, removed when the check ends)
  • Moderation records (warnings, timeouts, kicks and bans) with the moderator, the member and the reason given.
  • Who added the bot to each server, for the bot owner.

The bot reads messages to run its features: commands, auto-moderation, auto-responders, levels, translation, logging, starboards and counting. It does not save message text in its database. When a server has logging on with a message log channel and logs edited or deleted messages, the bot also keeps a short-lived copy of each member's messages (text, author, attachment names and links) in its cache for 7 days by default, only so a later edit or deletion can be shown in the server's log channel; the copy is removed as soon as the message is deleted (even when that deletion is not logged) or the time is up. Bots and webhooks are not copied. When logging is on, edited and deleted messages are posted to that server's own log channel. Ticket transcripts are posted to the server's channel or sent to you by DM, not kept by the bot.

The dashboard

  • You log in with Discord. The dashboard asks Discord only for your profile (ID, username, display name and avatar) and your list of servers with your permissions in them.
  • Your Discord login token is stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser for up to 7 days, not in the bot's database. Logging out ends it at Discord too.
  • The only cookies are that login cookie and a short-lived one used while you log in. There are no ads, analytics or tracking cookies.
  • Logins, logouts and settings changes are written to the dashboard's server log with your Discord user ID.
  • The dashboard is reached through Cloudflare, which carries the connection and sees your IP address.
  • The website and the dashboard load their fonts from Google Fonts, so your browser also connects to Google, which sees your IP address. No cookies are set for this.

Who else sees data

  • Discord, which hosts everything the bot posts.
  • Translation: text you translate, or that is posted in an auto-translate channel, goes to a translation server the bot owner runs (LibreTranslate). Results are cached for up to an hour.
  • Lookup commands send what you type to the site that answers: /search anime and /search manga to AniList, /search pokemon to PokéAPI, and /search urban to Urban Dictionary.
  • Social feeds that staff set up (RSS, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky, podcasts) are fetched from those sites. No member data is sent to them.

Data is never sold or shared for advertising.

How long data is kept

  • Data stays while the bot is in the server. If the bot is removed, its data is kept, so the settings come back if the bot is added again, until someone asks for it to be deleted.
  • Some records are removed automatically when they are no longer needed, for example finished captcha checks and a birthday you remove.
  • Backups are kept for up to six months, then deleted.

Your choices

  • You can ask for a copy of the data the bot holds about you, or for it to be deleted, by contacting . Deleting it resets things like your levels and balances.
  • Server staff can remove most of their server's data from the dashboard, or ask for everything about their server to be deleted.
  • You can log out of the dashboard at any time. You can also remove its access from Discord: User Settings → Authorized Apps.

Age

The bot is for Discord users only, so you must meet Discord's minimum age (13 in most countries).

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date.

# Changelog

What changed in Frost.Byte, newest first. Each entry is dated by when it landed on `main`; there are no version numbers yet. The full history is in the [commit log](https://github.com/MasstarVT/discord-bot/commits/main).

## 2026-11-26 · Personal info filter in Automod
- New Automod rule **Personal Info** (anti-doxxing): removes messages that share a phone number, street address, email address, social security number or card number. Turn it on with `/automod rule rule:Personal Info action:Delete & warn`, or on the dashboard's Auto-Moderation page. Ordinary numbers, dates, prices, Discord ids and links are left alone, and the mod log and deleted-message log blank the details out instead of repeating them.

## 2026-10-27 · Commands-only channels and maths in Counting
- New Automations preset **Commands Only**: `/automation create preset:Commands Only channel:#bot-commands` deletes every message in that channel that does not start with your custom-command prefix, so only commands are used there. Slash commands keep working, and members with the moderator roles (or the `role` you pick) can still talk. Also on the dashboard's Automations page.
- Counting accepts maths: `2+2`, `(3*4)-1` or `2^3` counts as the number it comes to. Sums that come to a fraction, such as `10/27`, are treated as chat and never reset the count.

## 2026-10-21 · Go-live posts for the Live Role
- The Live Role can now post in a channel when a member goes live, with a link to their Twitch or YouTube stream. Set it up with `/liverole announce channel:#live-now`, or on the dashboard; the message can be customised with `{url}`, `{platform}`, `{title}` and `{game}`, and `ping_role` pings a role such as @Stream Alerts with each post.

## 2026-10-20 · Auto Timestamps and a new site
- A new public site: the landing page opens every module to show its commands and default settings, runs sample commands with the bot's real replies, and lets you try the Levels settings. New `/docs` and `/changelog` pages list every module, command and change.
- New module **Auto Timestamps**: when a member types a time such as "friday 5pm" or "7pm EST", the bot replies with a Discord timestamp everyone reads in their own timezone. `/autotime enable` turns it on.
- Members with no timezone set are told how to pick a timezone role or use `/timezone set`.
- The dashboard's Audit Logs page lists every event that gets logged.

## 2026-10-19 · Public landing page and legal pages
- The dashboard got a new look, and the bot got a public landing page.
- Added a privacy policy and terms of service, plus trusted-proxy settings so the dashboard can be served publicly.
- Dependency security updates (js-yaml, brace-expansion, ip-address).

## 2026-10-18 · Honeypot channels
- Automod can now watch **honeypot channels**: whoever posts in one is softbanned (or banned, kicked or timed out) at once, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts. `/automod honeypot add` can create the channel and post a warning in it.

## 2026-10-17 · More reaction-role templates
- Reaction roles gained ready-made role sets: pronouns, colours, age ranges and more.

## 2026-10-16 · Timezones
- Added `/timestamp`, `/timezone` and timezone roles, so times show up in each member's own timezone.
- Timezone reaction-role templates in `/reactionrole` and the dashboard, and a timezone-roles editor on the dashboard's General page.
- Custom commands limited to certain roles are now hidden from members who can't run them.

## 2026-10-15 · Performance and fixes
- A performance pass across the bot, including buffered achievement message counts.
- Added `/owner`, which pings the bot owner.
- Fixed the bugs found in a full codebase review.

## 2026-10-14 · Counting
- New module **Counting**: members count up from 1 in turns; a wrong number or a double turn starts it over.
- The bot owner can see who added the bot to each server.

## 2026-10-13 · Dashboard access
- The dashboard shows only the servers you manage; the bot owner can manage, and join, any server the bot is in.
- Translation activity per channel on the dashboard.
- Setup commands can create the role or channel they ask for.
- Moderator commands now require default member permissions too.

## 2026-10-11 · The web dashboard
- Added the web dashboard: log in with Discord and change every module's settings in a browser.
- Manage saved embeds, custom commands, reminders, feeds, level rewards, the shop and achievements from it.
- Run giveaways and polls, build automations, manage reaction-role and ticket panels, and moderate members (XP and coins too) from the dashboard.
- An embed editor, member pickers and long-list paging.
- The bot itself was rebuilt for feature parity with MEE6, with the audited bugs fixed.

# Changelog

What changed in Frost.Byte, newest first. Each entry is dated by when it landed on `main`; there are no version numbers yet. The full history is in the [commit log](https://github.com/MasstarVT/discord-bot/commits/main).

## 2026-11-26 · Personal info filter in Automod
- New Automod rule **Personal Info** (anti-doxxing): removes messages that share a phone number, street address, email address, social security number or card number. Turn it on with `/automod rule rule:Personal Info action:Delete & warn`, or on the dashboard's Auto-Moderation page. Ordinary numbers, dates, prices, Discord ids and links are left alone, and the mod log and deleted-message log blank the details out instead of repeating them.

## 2026-10-27 · Commands-only channels and maths in Counting
- New Automations preset **Commands Only**: `/automation create preset:Commands Only channel:#bot-commands` deletes every message in that channel that does not start with your custom-command prefix, so only commands are used there. Slash commands keep working, and members with the moderator roles (or the `role` you pick) can still talk. Also on the dashboard's Automations page.
- Counting accepts maths: `2+2`, `(3*4)-1` or `2^3` counts as the number it comes to. Sums that come to a fraction, such as `10/27`, are treated as chat and never reset the count.

## 2026-10-21 · Go-live posts for the Live Role
- The Live Role can now post in a channel when a member goes live, with a link to their Twitch or YouTube stream. Set it up with `/liverole announce channel:#live-now`, or on the dashboard; the message can be customised with `{url}`, `{platform}`, `{title}` and `{game}`, and `ping_role` pings a role such as @Stream Alerts with each post.

## 2026-10-20 · Auto Timestamps and a new site
- A new public site: the landing page opens every module to show its commands and default settings, runs sample commands with the bot's real replies, and lets you try the Levels settings. New `/docs` and `/changelog` pages list every module, command and change.
- New module **Auto Timestamps**: when a member types a time such as "friday 5pm" or "7pm EST", the bot replies with a Discord timestamp everyone reads in their own timezone. `/autotime enable` turns it on.
- Members with no timezone set are told how to pick a timezone role or use `/timezone set`.
- The dashboard's Audit Logs page lists every event that gets logged.

## 2026-10-19 · Public landing page and legal pages
- The dashboard got a new look, and the bot got a public landing page.
- Added a privacy policy and terms of service, plus trusted-proxy settings so the dashboard can be served publicly.
- Dependency security updates (js-yaml, brace-expansion, ip-address).

## 2026-10-18 · Honeypot channels
- Automod can now watch **honeypot channels**: whoever posts in one is softbanned (or banned, kicked or timed out) at once, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts. `/automod honeypot add` can create the channel and post a warning in it.

## 2026-10-17 · More reaction-role templates
- Reaction roles gained ready-made role sets: pronouns, colours, age ranges and more.

## 2026-10-16 · Timezones
- Added `/timestamp`, `/timezone` and timezone roles, so times show up in each member's own timezone.
- Timezone reaction-role templates in `/reactionrole` and the dashboard, and a timezone-roles editor on the dashboard's General page.
- Custom commands limited to certain roles are now hidden from members who can't run them.

## 2026-10-15 · Performance and fixes
- A performance pass across the bot, including buffered achievement message counts.
- Added `/owner`, which pings the bot owner.
- Fixed the bugs found in a full codebase review.

## 2026-10-14 · Counting
- New module **Counting**: members count up from 1 in turns; a wrong number or a double turn starts it over.
- The bot owner can see who added the bot to each server.

## 2026-10-13 · Dashboard access
- The dashboard shows only the servers you manage; the bot owner can manage, and join, any server the bot is in.
- Translation activity per channel on the dashboard.
- Setup commands can create the role or channel they ask for.
- Moderator commands now require default member permissions too.

## 2026-10-11 · The web dashboard
- Added the web dashboard: log in with Discord and change every module's settings in a browser.
- Manage saved embeds, custom commands, reminders, feeds, level rewards, the shop and achievements from it.
- Run giveaways and polls, build automations, manage reaction-role and ticket panels, and moderate members (XP and coins too) from the dashboard.
- An embed editor, member pickers and long-list paging.
- The bot itself was rebuilt for feature parity with MEE6, with the audited bugs fixed.

## 2026-09-27 · Docker and CI
- Docker image, health endpoints, CI with GitHub Container Registry publishing, rollback and Dependabot.
- A LibreTranslate backend for translation, with back-off on rate limits.
- A failing event handler no longer restarts the bot; a shard that disconnects for good stops it cleanly.

## 2026-08-23 · README and license
- Added the README and the MIT license.

## 2026-06-11 · First version

Getting started

  1. Add Frost.Byte to a server where you have Manage Server: invite the bot. Its slash commands appear on their own.
  2. Switch on the modules you want. Run /module list to see them all and /module enable <name> to turn one on, or flip its switch on the dashboard. A module's setup command works while the module is still off, so you can configure it first.
  3. Fine-tune on the web. Log in to the dashboard with Discord, pick the server, and set channels, roles, messages and limits for each module.
  4. Check what members see. /help lists only the commands that member can run and that are switched on.

Who can run what

Everyone
Any member, in a server where the command's module is on.
Moderators
Members with the moderator permissions the command asks for, or a moderator role set with /modconfig.
Admins
Members with Manage Server. Discord hides these commands from everyone else, and the bot checks again.

# Changelog

What changed in Frost.Byte, newest first. Each entry is dated by when it landed on `main`; there are no version numbers yet. The full history is in the [commit log](https://github.com/MasstarVT/discord-bot/commits/main).

## 2026-11-26 · Personal info filter in Automod
- New Automod rule **Personal Info** (anti-doxxing): removes messages that share a phone number, street address, email address, social security number or card number. Turn it on with `/automod rule rule:Personal Info action:Delete & warn`, or on the dashboard's Auto-Moderation page. Ordinary numbers, dates, prices, Discord ids and links are left alone, and the mod log and deleted-message log blank the details out instead of repeating them.

## 2026-10-27 · Commands-only channels and maths in Counting
- New Automations preset **Commands Only**: `/automation create preset:Commands Only channel:#bot-commands` deletes every message in that channel that does not start with your custom-command prefix, so only commands are used there. Slash commands keep working, and members with the moderator roles (or the `role` you pick) can still talk. Also on the dashboard's Automations page.
- Counting accepts maths: `2+2`, `(3*4)-1` or `2^3` counts as the number it comes to. Sums that come to a fraction, such as `10/27`, are treated as chat and never reset the count.

## 2026-10-21 · Go-live posts for the Live Role
- The Live Role can now post in a channel when a member goes live, with a link to their Twitch or YouTube stream. Set it up with `/liverole announce channel:#live-now`, or on the dashboard; the message can be customised with `{url}`, `{platform}`, `{title}` and `{game}`, and `ping_role` pings a role such as @Stream Alerts with each post.

## 2026-10-20 · Auto Timestamps and a new site
- A new public site: the landing page opens every module to show its commands and default settings, runs sample commands with the bot's real replies, and lets you try the Levels settings. New `/docs` and `/changelog` pages list every module, command and change.
- New module **Auto Timestamps**: when a member types a time such as "friday 5pm" or "7pm EST", the bot replies with a Discord timestamp everyone reads in their own timezone. `/autotime enable` turns it on.
- Members with no timezone set are told how to pick a timezone role or use `/timezone set`.
- The dashboard's Audit Logs page lists every event that gets logged.

## 2026-10-19 · Public landing page and legal pages
- The dashboard got a new look, and the bot got a public landing page.
- Added a privacy policy and terms of service, plus trusted-proxy settings so the dashboard can be served publicly.
- Dependency security updates (js-yaml, brace-expansion, ip-address).

## 2026-10-18 · Honeypot channels
- Automod can now watch **honeypot channels**: whoever posts in one is softbanned (or banned, kicked or timed out) at once, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts. `/automod honeypot add` can create the channel and post a warning in it.

## 2026-10-17 · More reaction-role templates
- Reaction roles gained ready-made role sets: pronouns, colours, age ranges and more.

## 2026-10-16 · Timezones
- Added `/timestamp`, `/timezone` and timezone roles, so times show up in each member's own timezone.
- Timezone reaction-role templates in `/reactionrole` and the dashboard, and a timezone-roles editor on the dashboard's General page.
- Custom commands limited to certain roles are now hidden from members who can't run them.

## 2026-10-15 · Performance and fixes
- A performance pass across the bot, including buffered achievement message counts.
- Added `/owner`, which pings the bot owner.
- Fixed the bugs found in a full codebase review.

## 2026-10-14 · Counting
- New module **Counting**: members count up from 1 in turns; a wrong number or a double turn starts it over.
- The bot owner can see who added the bot to each server.

## 2026-10-13 · Dashboard access
- The dashboard shows only the servers you manage; the bot owner can manage, and join, any server the bot is in.
- Translation activity per channel on the dashboard.
- Setup commands can create the role or channel they ask for.
- Moderator commands now require default member permissions too.

## 2026-10-11 · The web dashboard
- Added the web dashboard: log in with Discord and change every module's settings in a browser.
- Manage saved embeds, custom commands, reminders, feeds, level rewards, the shop and achievements from it.
- Run giveaways and polls, build automations, manage reaction-role and ticket panels, and moderate members (XP and coins too) from the dashboard.
- An embed editor, member pickers and long-list paging.
- The bot itself was rebuilt for feature parity with MEE6, with the audited bugs fixed.

## 2026-09-27 · Docker and CI
- Docker image, health endpoints, CI with GitHub Container Registry publishing, rollback and Dependabot.
- A LibreTranslate backend for translation, with back-off on rate limits.
- A failing event handler no longer restarts the bot; a shard that disconnects for good stops it cleanly.

## 2026-08-23 · README and license
- Added the README and the MIT license.

## 2026-06-11 · First version
- The first version of the bot, including the games command and Scrabble.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 19 October 2026

This policy covers the Discord bot and its web dashboard. They are run by one person, the bot owner, not by a company. Questions or requests: Contact.

What the bot stores

The bot keeps only what its features need, in a database on the bot owner's own server:

  • Server settings that server staff choose: which modules are on, channels, roles, messages, embeds, custom commands, automations, panels and similar.
  • Discord IDs of servers, channels, roles, messages and members, so the bot knows where and to whom a feature applies.
  • Feature data about members, only for features a server turns on:
    • levels and XP, message counts and voice minutes
    • economy balances, items and boosts
    • achievements
    • birthdays (day and month, and the year only if you give it)
    • your time zone, if you set one
    • poll votes and giveaway entries
    • who invited whom, and when members joined or left
    • ticket owners and the reason you give when opening a ticket
    • temporary voice channel owners
    • captcha checks (a hashed answer and attempt count, removed when the check ends)
  • Moderation records (warnings, timeouts, kicks and bans) with the moderator, the member and the reason given.
  • Who added the bot to each server, for the bot owner.

The bot reads messages to run its features: commands, auto-moderation, auto-responders, levels, translation, logging, starboards and counting. It does not save message text in its database. When a server has logging on with a message log channel and logs edited or deleted messages, the bot also keeps a short-lived copy of each member's messages (text, author, attachment names and links) in its cache for 7 days by default, only so a later edit or deletion can be shown in the server's log channel; the copy is removed as soon as the message is deleted (even when that deletion is not logged) or the time is up. Bots and webhooks are not copied. When logging is on, edited and deleted messages are posted to that server's own log channel. Ticket transcripts are posted to the server's channel or sent to you by DM, not kept by the bot.

The dashboard

  • You log in with Discord. The dashboard asks Discord only for your profile (ID, username, display name and avatar) and your list of servers with your permissions in them.
  • Your Discord login token is stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser for up to 7 days, not in the bot's database. Logging out ends it at Discord too.
  • The only cookies are that login cookie and a short-lived one used while you log in. There are no ads, analytics or tracking cookies.
  • Logins, logouts and settings changes are written to the dashboard's server log with your Discord user ID.
  • The dashboard is reached through Cloudflare, which carries the connection and sees your IP address.
  • The website and the dashboard load their fonts from Google Fonts, so your browser also connects to Google, which sees your IP address. No cookies are set for this.

Who else sees data

  • Discord, which hosts everything the bot posts.
  • Translation: text you translate, or that is posted in an auto-translate channel, goes to a translation server the bot owner runs (LibreTranslate). Results are cached for up to an hour.
  • Lookup commands send what you type to the site that answers: /search anime and /search manga to AniList, /search pokemon to PokéAPI, and /search urban to Urban Dictionary.
  • Social feeds that staff set up (RSS, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky, podcasts) are fetched from those sites. No member data is sent to them.

Data is never sold or shared for advertising.

How long data is kept

  • Data stays while the bot is in the server. If the bot is removed, its data is kept, so the settings come back if the bot is added again, until someone asks for it to be deleted.
  • Some records are removed automatically when they are no longer needed, for example finished captcha checks and a birthday you remove.
  • Backups are kept for up to six months, then deleted.

Your choices

  • You can ask for a copy of the data the bot holds about you, or for it to be deleted, by contacting Contact. Deleting it resets things like your levels and balances.
  • Server staff can remove most of their server's data from the dashboard, or ask for everything about their server to be deleted.
  • You can log out of the dashboard at any time. You can also remove its access from Discord: User Settings → Authorized Apps.

Age

The bot is for Discord users only, so you must meet Discord's minimum age (13 in most countries).

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date.

Getting started

  1. Add Frost.Byte to a server where you have Manage Server: invite the bot. Its slash commands appear on their own.
  2. Switch on the modules you want. Run /module list to see them all and /module enable <name> to turn one on, or flip its switch on the dashboard. A module's setup command works while the module is still off, so you can configure it first.
  3. Fine-tune on the web. Log in to the dashboard with Discord, pick the server, and set channels, roles, messages and limits for each module.
  4. Check what members see. /help lists only the commands that member can run and that are switched on.

Who can run what

Everyone
Any member, in a server where the command's module is on.
Moderators
Members with the moderator permissions the command asks for, or a moderator role set with /modconfig.
Admins
Members with Manage Server. Discord hides these commands from everyone else, and the bot checks again.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 19 October 2026

This policy covers the Discord bot and its web dashboard. They are run by one person, the bot owner, not by a company. Questions or requests: Contact.

What the bot stores

The bot keeps only what its features need, in a database on the bot owner's own server:

  • Server settings that server staff choose: which modules are on, channels, roles, messages, embeds, custom commands, automations, panels and similar.
  • Discord IDs of servers, channels, roles, messages and members, so the bot knows where and to whom a feature applies.
  • Feature data about members, only for features a server turns on:
    • levels and XP, message counts and voice minutes
    • economy balances, items and boosts
    • achievements
    • birthdays (day and month, and the year only if you give it)
    • your time zone, if you set one
    • poll votes and giveaway entries
    • who invited whom, and when members joined or left
    • ticket owners and the reason you give when opening a ticket
    • temporary voice channel owners
    • captcha checks (a hashed answer and attempt count, removed when the check ends)
  • Moderation records (warnings, timeouts, kicks and bans) with the moderator, the member and the reason given.
  • Who added the bot to each server, for the bot owner.

The bot reads messages to run its features: commands, auto-moderation, auto-responders, levels, translation, logging, starboards and counting. It does not save message text in its database. When a server has logging on with a message log channel and logs edited or deleted messages, the bot also keeps a short-lived copy of each member's messages (text, author, attachment names and links) in its cache for 7 days by default, only so a later edit or deletion can be shown in the server's log channel; the copy is removed as soon as the message is deleted (even when that deletion is not logged) or the time is up. Bots and webhooks are not copied. When logging is on, edited and deleted messages are posted to that server's own log channel. Ticket transcripts are posted to the server's channel or sent to you by DM, not kept by the bot.

The dashboard

  • You log in with Discord. The dashboard asks Discord only for your profile (ID, username, display name and avatar) and your list of servers with your permissions in them.
  • Your Discord login token is stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser for up to 7 days, not in the bot's database. Logging out ends it at Discord too.
  • The only cookies are that login cookie and a short-lived one used while you log in. There are no ads, analytics or tracking cookies.
  • Logins, logouts and settings changes are written to the dashboard's server log with your Discord user ID.
  • The dashboard is reached through Cloudflare, which carries the connection and sees your IP address.
  • The website and the dashboard load their fonts from Google Fonts, so your browser also connects to Google, which sees your IP address. No cookies are set for this.

Who else sees data

  • Discord, which hosts everything the bot posts.
  • Translation: text you translate, or that is posted in an auto-translate channel, goes to a translation server the bot owner runs (LibreTranslate). Results are cached for up to an hour.
  • Lookup commands send what you type to the site that answers: /search anime and /search manga to AniList, /search pokemon to PokéAPI, and /search urban to Urban Dictionary.
  • Social feeds that staff set up (RSS, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky, podcasts) are fetched from those sites. No member data is sent to them.

Data is never sold or shared for advertising.

How long data is kept

  • Data stays while the bot is in the server. If the bot is removed, its data is kept, so the settings come back if the bot is added again, until someone asks for it to be deleted.
  • Some records are removed automatically when they are no longer needed, for example finished captcha checks and a birthday you remove.
  • Backups are kept for up to six months, then deleted.

Your choices

  • You can ask for a copy of the data the bot holds about you, or for it to be deleted, by contacting Contact. Deleting it resets things like your levels and balances.
  • Server staff can remove most of their server's data from the dashboard, or ask for everything about their server to be deleted.
  • You can log out of the dashboard at any time. You can also remove its access from Discord: User Settings → Authorized Apps.

Age

The bot is for Discord users only, so you must meet Discord's minimum age (13 in most countries).

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date.
